newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-PSV STAY TOP BY HOLDING FEYENOORD 0-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSV STAY TOP BY HOLDING FEYENOORD 0-0.

text.p: PSV Eindhoven maintained their three point lead in the Dutch league title on Sunday by clinging on for a 0-0 draw at Feyenoord's de Kuip stadium.
The match was more of a disappointment for Feyenoord, who remain second.

They extended their unbeaten home record against PSV to eleven seasons and restored some pride after their 7-2 drubbing in Eindhoven in October but with passionate home support and the bulk of the chances they are more likely to feel it was three points wasted.

PSV were severely depleted with four absentees, notably their Belgian striker Luc Nilis. The Dutch league's top-scorer with 15 goals ruled himself out on Friday with an ankle injury and left the PSV attack blunted with no central target for their wingers. Their creative midfielder Wim Jonk played but was hampered by a thigh strain.

The crowd bathed in the afternoon sun but for most of the first half that was all there way on offer as a packed midfield stifled all creativity. Officious refereeing also disturbed the flow of the match.

The game only came alive in the last ten minutes of the first half when Swede Henryk Larsson found the skill to break free from PSV's tight marking to set up two thunderous strikes from Jean Paul van Gastel and to send Gaston Taument free down the right flank.
Feyenoord again had more chances in the second half including a flashing header from Fernando Picun from a corner and a solid drive from Giovanni van Bronkhorst that was just wide of the left post.

But PSV's deep defending restricted Feyenoord to speculative shots for much of the match. Feyenoord maintained the pressure towards the end but Larsson's departure with 15 minutes to go left them with few ideas.

Feyenoord's defence, keenly marshalled by Dutch international Ronald Koeman, left PSV with only one decent shot from Wim Jonk who brought out a a good save from Feyenoord's keeper Ed de Goey. PSV counters led by Phillip Cocu and Boundewijn Zenden broke down without creating danger.
Taument, who leaves for Benfica at the end of the season, had a largely quiet game in his last Dutch classic. The right winger was substituted late in the second half.

The game was played in reasonable spirit despite a number of fouls. Only once was there any confrontation, a stand-off between Koeman and Cocu after the PSV player had brought down the Feyenoord defender.
PSV's busier defence picked up three yellow cards. Only Picun was booked for Feyenoord.

Fears of crowd trouble proved unfounded. Rotterdam police moved the kick-off time forward to prevent visiting PSV fans drinking through the afternoon. The thin sliver of PSV supporters continued a choral assault throughout the match but most of it was good-natured.

Feyenoord - 1-Ed de Goey, 2-George Boateng, 3-Fernando Picun, 4-Ronald Koeman, 5-Jean Paul van Gastel, 6-Henryk Larsson (12-Henk Vos 76), 7-Kees van Wonderen, 8-Gaston Taument (14-Tati Montoya 82), 9-Tomek Iwan, 10-Pablo Sanchez, 11-Giovanni van Bronkhorst.

PSV - 1-Ronald Waterreus, 2-Marcos Vampeta, 3-Jaap Stam, 4-Stan Valckx, 5-Arthur Numan, 6-Chris van der Weerden, 7-Zlejko Petrovic (18-Ovidiu Stinga 70), 8-Wim Jonk, 9-Marcelo, 10-Boudewijn Zenden, 11-Phillip Cocu.
